When a producing well is off-center in a bounded reservoir, boundary effects arrive unevenly because the distance from the well to different boundaries varies. This causes the pressure wave (or flow) from the well to interact with nearby boundaries first, while distant boundaries have a delayed effect. The uneven arrival of boundary effects can distort the pressure response and complicate the interpretation of well test data.

An **image well** is a mathematical representation used to simulate the effect of a boundary on the flow behavior. For a **sealing boundary** (such as a no-flow boundary), the image well is placed symmetrically across the boundary, at the same distance from the boundary as the actual well. This creates an equivalent "mirror" well that mimics the influence of the boundary on the pressure response. By including the image well in the analysis, the effects of the boundary can be accounted for, allowing for more accurate modeling of the reservoir behavior.
